setup.zh: 三天后，潮水要回来了。你不早不晚，混在人群里出来，空着手，一身泥。「捡到什么了？」「一撮土。」
setup.en: Three days later the tide is coming back. You come out neither early nor late, in the crowd, empty-handed and muddy. "Find anything?" "A pinch of earth."

recap.zh: 你空着手出了秘境；阿禾问你是不是长高了。腊月初七，周衡在告示栏贴出一张纸：外门大比，明日。
recap.en: You came out of the hidden realm empty-handed; Ah He asked if you'd grown. On the seventh of the twelfth month Zhou Heng posted a notice: the outer court contest, tomorrow.

zh: 三天后，秘境关闭。你空着手出来。
告示栏：外门大比，明日。头名，筑基丹一枚。
en: Three days on, the hidden realm closes. You come out empty-handed.
The notice board: the outer court contest, tomorrow. First place, one Foundation pill.

story.zh:
三天后，潮水要回来了。

外门弟子一个个从石门里出来。有的捧着一株灵草，捧得像捧着自己的性命；有的抱着一件破法器，锈得看不出原样，也宝贝得跟什么似的；更多的空着手，一身泥，一脸晦气。执事拿着一本名册，出来一个，勾一个。

观主玄沉子站在石门前，两只手拢在袖子里，还是三天前那个样子，像是这三天，他一步也没有挪过。

小满出来得不早也不晚，混在人群里，也是空着手，一身泥。

孙二狗出来得早。他那身灰袍从领口撕到了腰，一只袖子没了，脸上一道一道的泥，额角上肿着一个青包，走路一瘸一拐。可他没哭。

小满迎上去，问：「怎么了？」

孙二狗道：「右边……人太多了。挤。挤到第二间石室的时候，地上有个坑，我给挤下去了。」他咧了咧嘴，一咧，额角的青包便疼，「坑不深，一丈来深。上面的人都在抢一株灵草，没人听见我喊。」

小满道：「那你怎么上来的？」

孙二狗道：「自己爬的。」他伸出两只手来给小满看，十个指头的指甲，劈了七个，「坑壁滑，爬上去，滑下来，爬上去，又滑下来。我数了，滑下来十九回。第二十回，上来了。」

小满看着那十个劈了的指甲，半天没说话。

孙二狗又从怀里摸出一样东西，双手递过来，是那根萝卜，完完整整的，一口都没有咬过。他道：「沈师兄，还你。」

小满道：「你在坑里一天一夜，没吃？」

孙二狗道：「我娘说，人家给的东西，要还的。」他顿了一顿，脸又红了，「……我饿的时候，就闻一闻。」

小满没有接那根萝卜。他把孙二狗的手推回去，道：「你留着。那是利息。」

孙二狗愣道：「什么利息？」

小满道：「你滑下来十九回，第二十回上来了。这个，值一根萝卜的利息。」

孙二狗没听懂，可他又很郑重地点了点头，把萝卜揣回怀里，跟那个护身符揣在一处，一瘸一拐地走了。

小满望着他的背影。那个背影瘦得像一根竹竿，风一吹便要倒的样子，可是走了一路，没有倒。

阿禾早出来了，蹲在河滩上一块石头旁边，看见他，站起身来，拍了拍身上的泥，问：「捡到什么了？」

小满说：「一撮土。」

阿禾道：「……土？」

小满说：「土。」

小满问她：「你呢？捡到什么了？」

阿禾道：「什么也没捡到。右边第三间石室，有一株灵草，我到的时候，给人拔了。」

小满道：「那你进去三天，做什么了？」

阿禾想了想，道：「喊了两回。」

小满道：「喊什么？」

阿禾道：「第二间石室门口，地上第三块石板，踩上去会翻。地图上画着的。两回有人要踩，我喊了一声『别踩第三块』。」

小满道：「他们听了？」

阿禾道：「一个听了。一个没来得及听，给后头的人一挤，掉下去了，一丈来深。我给人群推着往前走，回不去。后来听说，是自己爬上来的。」

小满想起孙二狗那十个劈了的指甲，没有说话。

阿禾又道：「听了的那一个，我记了一笔。」

小满道：「记什么？」

阿禾道：「利息。」她顿了一顿，面无表情地补了一句，「我喊了一嗓子，救他一条腿。一条腿，利息不能少。」

小满看着她。她鼻头冻得通红，灰袍的下摆全是泥，那张脸从头到尾一点表情都没有，可小满知道，那一个没来得及听的，她一定也记了一笔，记的不是利息。

阿禾盯着他看了一会儿，从怀里掏出小本子，翻开来：「地图的利息，两块灵石。」

小满说：「我没钱。」

阿禾道：「那记着。」

小满说：「记着。」

阿禾合上本子，走了两步，又回过头来，上上下下打量了他一回，道：「你是不是……长高了？」

小满心里咯噔一下。他缩了缩脖子，又缩了缩肩膀，把自己往矮里缩了一寸，道：「秘境里冷，缩了三天，一出来，伸开了。」

阿禾「哦」了一声，又看了他一眼。她那一眼看得很久，久到小满以为她要掏本子了。她却没有掏，转身走了。

小满站在那里，把一身的灵气往里收，收得紧紧的，收成一只漏勺的样子。他练了一路，从石缝练到石门，如今收得像模像样了：外头看来，还是那个练气二层、下下之资的沈小满。他心想：从今往后，这一门功夫，比什么都要紧。
story.en:
Three days later the tide was coming back.

The outer disciples came out of the stone door one by one. Some held a single herb as if holding their own lives; some hugged a broken tool rusted past recognising, treasured all the same; most came out empty-handed, muddy, glum. A steward with a roll book ticked each one off as he came.

Abbot Xuanchenzi stood before the stone door, hands in his sleeves, just as he had been three days before, as if in those three days he had not moved a step.

Xiaoman came out neither early nor late, mixed in with the crowd, empty-handed too, and muddy.

Sun Ergou came out early. His grey robe was torn from collar to waist, one sleeve gone, mud streaked on his face, a blue lump on his temple, and he limped. But he wasn't crying.

Xiaoman went to meet him. "What happened?"

"On the right… too many people. Pushing. At the second chamber there was a pit in the floor and I got pushed in." He grinned; grinning hurt the lump. "Not deep, ten feet or so. Everyone up top was fighting over one herb; nobody heard me shout."

"Then how did you get out?"

"Climbed." He held out both hands; of ten fingernails, seven were split. "The sides were slick — climb up, slide down, climb up, slide down again. I counted: I slid down nineteen times. The twentieth, I got out."

Xiaoman looked at those ten split nails and said nothing for a long while.

Sun Ergou took something from his coat and held it out in both hands: the radish, whole, not one bite taken. "Brother Shen, I'm giving it back."

"A day and a night in the pit and you didn't eat it?"

"My ma says what people give you, you give back." He paused and went red again. "…When I was hungry, I smelled it."

Xiaoman didn't take the radish. He pushed Sun Ergou's hands back. "Keep it. That's interest."

"What interest?"

"You slid down nineteen times and the twentieth you got out. That's worth a radish in interest."

Sun Ergou didn't understand, but he nodded very gravely again, tucked the radish back into his coat beside the charm, and limped off.

Xiaoman watched him go. The back was thin as a bamboo pole, as if a gust would knock it over — but it went all the way and didn't fall.

Ah He had come out long before and was squatting by a rock on the riverbank. Seeing him, she stood and brushed off the mud. "Find anything?"

"A pinch of earth," said Xiaoman.

"…Earth?"

"Earth."

Xiaoman asked her, "And you? Find anything?"

"Nothing. There was a herb in the third chamber on the right; by the time I got there someone had pulled it."

"Then what did you do in there three days?"

Ah He thought. "Shouted twice."

"Shouted what?"

"At the door of the second chamber, the third flagstone flips when you step on it. It's on the map. Twice someone was about to step on it and I shouted 'not the third one.'"

"Did they listen?"

"One listened. One didn't have time — got pushed from behind and fell in, ten feet or so. The crowd swept me on; I couldn't go back. I heard later he climbed out by himself."

Xiaoman thought of Sun Ergou's ten split nails and said nothing.

"The one who listened," Ah He went on, "I wrote down."

"Wrote what?"

"Interest." She paused and added without expression, "One shout, saved him a leg. A leg — the interest can't be small."

Xiaoman looked at her. Nose frozen red, the hem of her robe all mud, not a flicker of expression on her face from start to finish — but Xiaoman knew she had written down the one who didn't have time to listen, too, and what she'd written wasn't interest.

Ah He studied him a while, took out her notebook and opened it. "Interest on the map: two stones."

"I've no money," said Xiaoman.

"Then it's on the books."

"On the books."

Ah He closed the notebook, took two steps, turned back, and looked him up and down. "Have you… grown?"

Xiaoman's heart jolted. He hunched his neck, hunched his shoulders, shrank himself an inch. "Cold in the hidden realm. I was hunched up three days; came out and stretched."

"Oh," said Ah He, and gave him another look. It lasted so long Xiaoman thought she'd take out the notebook. She didn't; she turned and went.

Xiaoman stood there, drawing all his qi inward, pulling it tight, into the shape of a skimmer. He had practised all the way, from the crack in the rock to the stone door, and now he had it passably: from outside, still the same Shen Xiaoman, second level of Qi Refining, bottom of the bottom. He thought: from now on, this is the art that matters more than any.

label.en: Enough for today — the contest is tomorrow

story.zh:
**阿禾的小本子**

冬月初一。借沈小满地图一张。利息两块。

冬月初一。自己背地图。花半块。花一夜。

冬月初一。他没往右走。

冬月初二。右边第三间石室，有一株灵草，给人拔了。我没拔着。

冬月初三。他出来了。说捡了一撮土。

冬月初三。他长高了。他说是冷的。

冬月初三。冷的人，缩着才对。

冬月初三。这一条，不收利息。

腊月初七一早，周衡在外门的告示栏上贴了一张纸，纸上写着：**外门大比，明日。头名，筑基丹一枚。**
story.en:
**Ah He's little notebook**

First day, eleventh month. Lent Shen Xiaoman one map. Interest two.

First day, eleventh month. Learned the map myself. Cost half. Cost a night.

First day, eleventh month. He didn't go right.

Second day, eleventh month. Third chamber on the right, one herb, someone pulled it. I didn't get it.

Third day, eleventh month. He came out. Says he found a pinch of earth.

Third day, eleventh month. He's grown. He says it's the cold.

Third day, eleventh month. A cold person ought to be hunched up.

Third day, eleventh month. No interest on this one.

Early on the seventh of the twelfth month, Zhou Heng pasted a sheet on the outer court's notice board. It read: **Outer court contest: tomorrow. First place: one Foundation pill.**
